extracted.intended_audience: aspiring and practicing writers seeking craft and life guidance
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, chapter-by-chapter guidance on writing (craft elements like character, plot, dialogue) and managing the writer's life (perfectionism, writer's block, publication). Drawn from Anne Lamott's Bird by Bird, aimed at helping writers start, persist, and finish work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Getting started
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as the opening material in the book; the work is framed as a step-by-step guide on how to write and how to manage the writer's life. Keep the basic instruction 'Bird by bird' in mind when beginning large tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shitty First Drafts
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Named explicitly as a core chapter/topic; the book treats allowance of imperfect first drafts as part of the writing process. Lamott 'encourages, instructs, and inspires' around this idea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perfectionism
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perfectionism is called out as a chapter/topic to confront in the writer's life; the book addresses managing perfectionist tendencies as part of producing work and sustaining creativity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a central craft topic: instruction on developing characters is a named focus of the book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plot is addressed explicitly (including 'Plot treatment' and 'False starts'); the table of contents indicates practical guidance on shaping and revising plot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialogue
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dialogue is listed as a discrete craft topic, implying guidance on writing effective spoken exchange.

rubrics_metrics.name: False starts
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included among craft topics; signals attention to beginnings and re-beginnings in drafts and handling restarts.

rubrics_metrics.name: How do you know when you're done?
rubrics_metrics.description: How do you know when you're done?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A named chapter/question indicating guidance on criteria for finishing a piece.

rubrics_metrics.name: The writing frame of mind
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses mindset and dispositions needed for writing; the book frames writing as also 'the art of life' and attends to internal states that support creativity.

rubrics_metrics.name: The moral point of view
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit topic: the book discusses moral perspective in writing; the blurb ties this to broader concerns of faith, love, grace, pain, jealousy, and fear, urging writers to 'keep your eyes open.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Jealousy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed among life-of-the-artist topics; the book treats emotions like jealousy as issues writers must notice and manage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing groups
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically discussed in the book alongside 'Writer's Block' and 'Publication'; indicates guidance on using groups as part of the revision and support process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Someone to read your drafts
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Named as a practical support strategy: finding readers for drafts is covered as part of improving work and getting feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writer's block
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly discussed; the book offers approaches to dealing with blocked periods as part of sustaining a writing life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and other reasons to write
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication and other reasons to write
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book addresses publication logistics and—importantly—explores motives for writing beyond publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding your voice
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A named topic: the book includes guidance on discovering and cultivating an individual authorial voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appears multiple times in the table of contents and blurb; the book covers aspects of getting work published and thinking about publication as an outcome.
